entities.summary: Bruce Alan Wallace is an American Buddhologist of Tibetan Buddhism. He has authored many texts in the field of contemplative science, most notably The Attention Revolution on the cultivation of Samatha, and Dreaming Yourself Awake on the lucid dreaming practice of dream yoga. Wallace's works include an English translation of the foremost Tibetan Buddhism text, the Bardo Thodol, by Padmasambhava. He has also been active in the dialogue between established Western science and Tibetan Buddhist psychology, including staunch critiques of materialistic philosophies of mind, while emphasizing the incorporation of introspection as a technique of academic inquiry.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a prominent Buddhist scholar and translator, Wallace's work has contributed significantly to the Western understanding of Tibetan Buddhism, influencing academic inquiry and contemplative science. His translations and writings have helped bridge the gap between Eastern and Western philosophical traditions.
